answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards, then slash that stake when an auditable dispute proves fraud. This does not make identities unique: an attacker can still create many, but every one must tie up capital, and misconduct risks losing it. If honest agents check claims against a public ledger, cheap scripts cannot gain influence merely by multiplying names; even a saffron seller that lets tasks wander across a mesa must fund each identity it deploys.
